items.title: How to speak whale: AI uses eight to ten click sequences to predict sperm whales' feeding dives
items.excerpt: Project CETI researchers fed sperm whale coda recordings into machine-learning models and found that a run of roughly eight to ten click sequences predicts when a whale is about to begin a deep foraging dive.

items.title: Researchers develop AI tool to map microRNA binding sites on circular RNAs
items.excerpt: Pusan National University's circMAC deep-learning model (Briefings in Bioinformatics) combines attention, Mamba and convolution layers with circular padding to estimate per-nucleotide microRNA binding on full-length circular RNAs, outperforming RNA language models.

items.title: AI agents can form political camps, and changing their conversation partners does little to soften their views
items.excerpt: In a Nature Communications study from Tsinghua University, 1,000 LLM agents given political positions spontaneously polarized into like-minded camps; rewiring partners barely helped, while prompting receptiveness cut polarization by 11.8%.

items.title: Low-power neural chip reads brain signals to identify cognitive and emotional states
items.excerpt: EPFL's LogSync implantable chip (IEEE JSSC) measures oscillations and cross-region synchrony, and an on-chip machine-learning algorithm uses those network signals to classify cognitive and emotional states; tested on prior human recordings and rats.

items.title: Computer scientists build tech tools to find experiments, detect citation 'hallucinations'
items.excerpt: NYU's Dennis Shasha and students describe two web-hosted AI systems in the journal Information: Hallucination Nerd checks whether a paper's claims are supported by its citations, and Protocol Nerd helps scientists find suitable experimental protocols.

items.title: LLMs show a human-like double standard when judging others' reasoning
items.excerpt: A Harvard preprint (Vitali and Banaji) replicating a 2019 Psychological Science study finds GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet update probabilities in a roughly Bayesian way, yet judge a person who reasons the same way more harshly than humans do.

items.title: Nvidia, UW Institute for Protein Design unveil open-source protein design AI model
items.excerpt: The UW Institute for Protein Design and Nvidia released RFD4-Proteina, an open generative model that merges RosettaFold Diffusion with Proteina-Complexa; Manchester researchers already used it to design active enzymes for a step in lenacapavir synthesis.

items.title: PerturbAI and OpenAI launch AI reasoning agents for biomedical discovery
items.excerpt: PerturbAI and OpenAI are pairing reasoning agents with PerturbAI's proprietary causal perturbation data, expanding their partnership into a joint drug-target discovery effort.

items.title: AI could turn scientific papers into research assistants
items.excerpt: An AI 'virtual author' built from a paper can help scientists apply its methods to new data, though it does not match the human author's expertise.

items.title: AI proved the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. What happens now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this AI-generated proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis has been unpacked by human experts, and one mathematician calls the implications 'staggering.'

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT historian Benjamin Lindquist discusses how early AI researchers deliberately built randomness and irrationality into models meant to mimic human creativity.

items.title: Q&A: The 'collision' between AI, your brain, and society
items.excerpt: MIT Professor Eric So argues in his book 'The Collision' that heavy AI use can cause cognitive atrophy, with people failing to develop and retain essential thinking skills.

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to map nearly 10,000 reactions in CO2-to-fuel conversion on copper catalysts, uncovering pathways traditional models missed and sharply improving predictions.

items.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world's forest types
items.excerpt: DeepMind's Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 is a global 10-meter AI map that separates Earth's land into six forest and land-use types, plus an annual time series.

items.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
items.excerpt: Google Antigravity serves as an agentic science workbench that discovers, structurally evaluates and prioritizes candidate antimicrobial peptides in hours.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research describes Earth AI geospatial agents that combine its planetary foundation models with reasoning to analyze environmental and societal problems.

items.title: Google launches $150,000 AI competition to reduce quantum computing demands
items.excerpt: Google Quantum AI launched a $150,000 Kaggle competition for AI methods that design smaller, more efficient quantum circuits for calculations.

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical computing approach detects deepfake videos with a claimed 97.8% accuracy, using less energy than digital neural networks of similar performance.
